# Controlled media fixtures

`media/` contains project-generated FFmpeg test patterns and a 440 Hz sine tone. No public channel or third-party recording is bundled. H.264 Constrained Baseline level 3.0, 320×180 at 24 fps, AAC-LC mono 48 kHz, eight seconds, two-second segments. Both MPEG-TS and fMP4 HLS variants are available.

`/hls/live.m3u8` rotates these four TS segments through a sliding window with increasing sequence numbers and explicit discontinuities each eight seconds. It exercises real continuous decode without unbounded fixture storage. The fixture's original encoded timestamps restart at each marked cycle. Its monotonic wall clock can be injected in tests.

Regenerate with `node scripts/generate-fixtures.mjs` using the development-only `ffmpeg-static` dependency. An optional first argument selects an already-installed FFmpeg executable. `media/generation.json` records encoder version, exact arguments, fixture seed, byte sizes, and SHA-256 hashes. Different encoder versions can change encoded bytes; decode behavior must be retested after regeneration. FFmpeg is not bundled in application releases.

Start the loopback fault server with `node scripts/fixture-server.mjs` (default port 17840), or import `startFixtureServer()` for an ephemeral port. Actual decoded-media paths: `/hls/master.m3u8`, `/media/index.m3u8`, `/hls/extensionless`, `/media/fmp4.m3u8`. Fault paths include `/fault/headers-stall`, `/fault/body-stall`, `/fault/delayed.m3u8`, `/fault/segment-stall.m3u8`, `/fault/403`, `/fault/429`, `/fault/503`, `/fault/disconnect`, and `/fault/malformed.m3u8`.

`/hls/key-map.m3u8`, `/hls/key`, and `/hls/map` exercise URI/resource handling only. That syntax fixture is not encrypted valid video and cannot prove decoding. Eight-second VOD does not prove live-edge recovery, Android behavior, or a two-hour native soak.

Actual protocol fixtures are separate under `media/protocol/`: generate them with `node scripts/generate-protocol-fixtures.mjs`, which reads the existing owned media without regenerating it. Seed `owned-aes-range-v1-sequence100` uses a publicly disclosed fixed 16-byte AES key, CBC/PKCS7 and explicit sequence IVs100–103 to encrypt four valid MPEG-TS segments. `/protocol/aes/master.m3u8` points to a relative variant; its key and encrypted segments also retain relative paths/query parameters. This is test material, never a production key.

`/protocol/range/index.m3u8` references a valid concatenation of the owned fMP4 initialization and four segments. Its initialization map has an explicit byte range at0, its first media segment has an explicit offset, and subsequent offsets are implicit. `/protocol/resources/ranges.mp4` serves actual bounded206/Content-Range responses. Strict allowlisted routes serve only these generated resources. `media/protocol/generation.json` records input/output byte lengths and SHA256 hashes; identical existing source bytes give deterministic outputs. Preserve the original `media/generation.json` and fixtures during active tests/soaks. The Windows receipt at `artifacts/media-protocol/2026-10-10T19-53-09.984Z/report.json` used the original `tests/fixtures/protocol` path; these same hash-verified generated bytes were moved under the existing binary-media tooling exclusion afterward. Its decoder observation remains tied to those exact bytes and executable, not a subsequent build.

Windows protocol runner: `node tests/native/media-protocol-smoke.mjs <explicit-executable-path>`. Coordinate an idle native-test window first. It copies that exact executable into a unique `artifacts/media-protocol/<timestamp>` directory, isolates data/WebView profile, imports a controlled HTTP catalog through the actual UI and checks AES/key fetching, map206 and explicit/implicit media ranges with decoded frames/time progression. It records executable/fixture hashes, runtime, resource requests and awaited native-exit/server cleanup. It does not rebuild the app or contact public providers, TVs or Android devices; a pass certifies only the recorded binary/runtime/fixture combination. Current source changes require fresh binary proof separately.

Windows native continuous-decoder runner: `node scripts/windows-soak.mjs --duration 7200 --exe src-tauri/target/debug/tmg-tv.exe`. A short probe can use `--duration 20 --interval 2`. Reports and JSONL samples are isolated under `artifacts/windows-soak/<timestamp>/`; they identify executable SHA-256, fixture seed, encoder, runtime, observed duration, decoded frames, media time, browser heap, and memory/handles for the owned application and CDP-reported WebView processes. Short probes explicitly record `fullTwoHourRun: false`. Memory readings do not establish a device budget or prove Android acceptance. The child gets an isolated data directory and loopback debug endpoint; production launch arguments are unaffected.

HD profiles are generated separately with `node scripts/generate-profile-fixtures.mjs [explicit-encoder]`, under a new timestamped `media/profiles/` directory. Existing fixtures stay intact. The three owned patterns are 720p/30 H.264 Main3.1, 1080p/30 Main4.0, and 1080p/60 High4.2, each eight seconds with stereo AAC and both TS/fMP4 segmentation. The declared 2,500/5,000/8,000 video kbps are encoder target/max-rate settings, not measured delivered bitrates. The receipt preserves encoder executable SHA/version, commands, all bytes/hashes and the public test-pattern seed. Encoder version changes can change fixture bytes. Generation alone establishes no device capability.

Run `node tests/native/profile-smoke.mjs <explicit-executable> <timestamped-profile-root>` in the sole Windows native-test window. It imports all six cases through the actual UI, checks exact dimensions and advancing decoded frames/time, and requires native exit code zero and fixture cleanup. It proves short profile decoding only, without audio observation, endurance, memory ceilings or Android claims. The Windows continuous runner can select a hash-verified generated profile with `--profile-root <timestamped-profile-root> --profile-id 720p30|1080p30|1080p60`; coordinate an idle window first. Samples now retain CDP process subtype, aggregate DOM/listener/document metrics and worker target counts without target URLs. Those are observable browser totals, not counts of GenX-owned engines or timers. Profile/diagnostic changes do not retrospectively add fields to earlier soak evidence.
